AI-Generated (88 words): Optional Ready-Made Gut Stacks
I don't think there's one supplement stack (a set of supplements you take together) that heals everyone's gut, and no stack can do the phases above for you. So do those first, in order, and only go after bugs and parasites if your symptoms are still there after you've changed your diet. Then a stack can help with the rebuilding in Phase 5, once you're clear of infection and it's time to feed the good bacteria again.
AI-Generated (17 words): That said, some people want a ready-made stack rather than buying every ingredient for it separately.

AI-Generated (58 words): Ruscio's Leaky Gut Support Kit has a probiotic and two gut lining products, one of them glutamine, but no prebiotic, so it's more for when leaky gut is your main problem. Finally, Designs for Health GI Revive is only gut-lining nutrients and herbs, so you'd still need a probiotic and a prebiotic with it.

AI-Generated (99 words): Start any kit at a low dose and build up as your gut gets used to it. The prebiotic part especially can give you gas at first, since gas is what your bacteria make when they ferment the fiber or resistant starch, and a new probiotic can bloat you or upset your stomach for a while.
You'll also find "gut cleanse" stacks, built around oregano oil, wormwood, black walnut, berberine or other antimicrobial herbs. They kill bugs, like the herbal antibiotics in Phase 3, so they're only for when changing your diet hasn't cleared your symptoms.
AI-Generated (26 words): If your immune system is weak, some probiotics could be risky since they're live bacteria that need to be kept in check to prevent overgrowth.
AI-Generated (26 words): If you have an IBD flare, cancer or another serious illness, work out what to take with your doctor instead of putting a stack together yourself.
